text:
Mari J.: Heads up — saw a spike of gpu pods Pending in us-west1 around 06:10. CA kept adding nodes to the slice pool but the jobs still stayed Pending.
Kevin L.: which nodepool? any config changes overnight?
Mari J.: nodepool= gpu-heavy-rtg (full GPUs, no taints), and gpu-slice-burst (time-slice friendly). We enabled MIG on a subset last week. Looks like scheduler keeps landing on slice pool which doesn't satisfy nodeSelector for full-GPU jobs.
Frank C.: can you paste the pod failure reason?
Mari J.: sure, from kubectl describe: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   3m    default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 4 node(s) had taint {exclusive=true:NoSchedule}: NoSchedule.
```
Kevin L.: aha — taint and nodeSelector mismatch. But curious why CA chose to scale gpu-slice-burst first. It should prefer full-GPU nodepool for pods that request 1 GPU.
Leah S.: two noticeable behaviours we've seen: (1) CA balancing + scale-up policies bias towards cheaper pool (slice) because it satisfies CPU/memory fit, (2) binpacking mode can leave pods waiting for a full GPU slot while many fractional slots are spread across nodes.
Mari J.: proposal: enforce stronger nodeAffinity on full-GPU workloads and taint full nodes with exclusive=true:NoSchedule; then set tolerations only on full jobs. That will force CA to scale the right pool.
Frank C.: small config snippet we used before for full jobs: 
```
spec:
  containers:
  - name: trainer
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
  tolerations:
  - key: "exclusive"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeSelector:
    gpu-class: "full"
```
Kevin L.: throwing fractional requests at schedulers won't fix MIG mismatch: for MIG we need device-plugin + nodes pre-provisioned with the right MIG profile. So two clean choices: (A) dedicate a pool with MIG profiles and label it, (B) keep full-GPU pool for monolithic jobs.
Leah S.: also bump CA config: increase --scale-down-unneeded-time to avoid premature teardown of slice nodes that CA thinks are unused but actually hold cached docker layers for GPU workloads. We had thundering restarts after scale-down.
autoscaler-bot: Cluster Autoscaler: scaled up 2 nodes in gpu-slice-burst (reason: 5 pending pods, insufficient resources).
Mari J.: plan I'm going to run: create a new nodepool gpu-exclusive-rtg with taint exclusive=true:NoSchedule and label gpu-class=full. Update our helm chart to add toleration only for batch/training jobs. Also add an admission webhook check to prevent accidental toleration on low-priority pods.
Kevin L.: +1. Also add a CA annotation to prefer node pool for volumetyped workloads. We should test scale-up latency end-to-end before rolling. @Leah S. can you help tune the CA flags?
Leah S.: yes — I'll try: set --balance-similar-node-groups=false and set --max-node-provision-time to 8m, and bump max-scale-up-rate for gpu pools. Will measure cost impact.
Mari J.: note on cost: slice nodes ~30% cheaper per-hour but add ~2x latency for setups that need full GPU (because of fallback). If we keep mixing, we pay for extra scale operations. Documenting tradeoffs in the PR.
Frank C.: suggest adding a smoke test that creates a pending job and asserts CA scales the correct pool within X minutes. Saves a late-night pager.
Mari J.: agreed — will add smoke test and open PR now.
Kevin L.: thanks everyone. Please drop the PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
Leah S.: will follow up with billing delta after one day of the new pool.
Mari J.: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/pull/4723 — contains new nodepool + toleration changes.
Kevin L.: reviewing now.
autoscaler-bot: Cluster Autoscaler: scaled down 1 node in gpu-slice-burst (reason: unneeded after 18m).
Mari J.: closing loop — monitoring alert for Pending GPU pods lowered after 30m. Will watch for regressions. :white_check_mark:
